messages.subject: scatterplot from molten? dataframe
parts:
Apologies for the noob question. This has probably been answered over
and over, but I can't think of the right keywords to search for.

I want to make a scatterplot using some data from a database query. It
comes like this:

> res = dbGetQuery()
> res
prop val fctr
x 0.1 a
y 0.3 a
x 0.8 b
y 1.3 b

prop is the variable to be plotted (on the x or the y axis,
respectively); val is the variable's value; fctr is a factor with a
couple of levels.

I know I can do this:

qplot(subset(res, prop=="x")$val,
subset(res, prop=="y")$val,
geom="jitter")

But this doesn't let me do a qplot(data=res, colour=fctr), because x
and y are two independent variables, i.e., I ignore the fact that
they're coming from the same dataframe res. I think that one solution
is to reshape the dataframe, but that seems like a kluge.

Thanks in advance.

messages.subject: Re: scatterplot from molten? dataframe
parts:
Hadley, thanks for thinking about this. The dataframe. can be made to
have four cols:

id prop fct val
1 x a 0.1
1 y b 0.3

id is a person, prop is the measurement of the person's w.r.t. the
factor fct. Suppose the cross-product prop X fct yields 6 combinations
(prop can be x or y, fct can be a, b, or c). Then every id (person) is
guaranteed to have been measured w.r.t each of these 6 combinations
exactly once.

In other words, every point (x,y) in the scatterplot is a person being
measured on x and on y w.r.t. to some factor fct, and every person
should have exactly 3 such points because there are 3 factors.

messages.subject: Re: scatterplot from molten? dataframe
parts:
I think reshaping is the only way here. Assuming your data is in a
dataframe called res:

qplot(x, y, data = cast(res, id + fct ~ prop), colour = fct)

Charlotte
